Name: Object Import Map
Author: aedenthorn
Description:
This mod lets you use a tmx map file to import the following items directly onto the current map:

[list]
[*]Fully-grown trees
[*]Ordinary objects
[*]Fully-grown crops
[*]Planted seeds
[*]Pre-tuned flute blocks (and preset tones using [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/10934]Advanced Flute Blocks[/url]﻿)
[*]Preset drum blocks
[*]Flooring tiles
[*]Train Tracks (using the [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/10927]Train Tracks[/url]﻿ mod)
[/list]
To import a premade object import map:

[list=1]
[*]Place the map in this mod's assets folder and name it [b]import.tmx[/b].
[*]Go to the target map in-game and type [b]/importmap[/b] and hit [b]Enter[/b].
[/list]
If you want to empty the map first, you can type [b]/nukemap[/b] and press [b]Enter[/b]. This nukes pretty much everything on the map minus NPCs and buildings.

[size=5][b]Creating Maps[/b][/size]

This part assumes you know [url=https://stardewvalleywiki.com/Modding:Maps#Using_Tiled]how to use Tiled with Stardew Valley maps[/url].

Copy the map file for the target map into the mod's assets folder and add layers according to what type of thing you want to import.

Add the corresponding tilesheets as well and link them to the png files in this mod's assets folder.

You may have to redirect the existing tilesheets to files in this mod's assets folder in order to make them show properly.

Add the proper tiles from the proper tilesheet to the proper layer and save the map.

There is an example map called EXAMPLE_import.tmx file included in the assets folder that you can use as a guide.


[b][size=4]Trees[/size][/b]

To add trees, create a tile layer called [b]Trees[/b] and use the Paths tilesheet to add trees according to the tree symbols on the Paths tilesheet.  Tree types are as follows:

[list]
[*]1 - Oak
[*]2 - Maple
[*]3 - Pine
[*]6 - Desert Palm
[*]7 - Ginger Island Palm
[*]9 - Mahogany
[/list]

[b][size=4]Objects[/size][/b]

To add objects, create a tile layer called [b]Objects [/b]and add tiles using a tilesheet with the [b]springobjects.png[/b] as its source.

Lots of objects should not really be spawned this way, but some of them turn out okay.


[size=4][b]Crops and Seed[/b][/size][b][size=4]s[/size][/b]

To add crops and seeds, use the [b]Objects[/b] layer as above and add the corresponding tile from [b]springobjects.png[/b].

Seed packets spawned this way will be planted, and produce that has a corresponding seed will be planted fully-grown.


[size=4][b]Flute and Drum Blocks[/b][/size]

For flute blocks, create a tile layer called [b]FluteBlocks[/b] and add tiles using a tilesheet with the [b]fluteblocks.png[/b] file as its source.

Flute block tunes can be changed if you have Advanced Flute Blocks installed. The five rows of tiles in the tilesheet correspond to the following tones:

[list]
[*]flute
[*]toyPiano
[*]crystal
[*]clam_tone
[*]toolCharge
[/list]
Note that some of these tones are pitched differently from each other.

For drum blocks, create a tile layer called [b]DrumBlocks[/b] and add tiles using a tilesheet with the [b]drumblocks.png[/b] file as its source.

Drum block indexes (1-7) correspond to the seven drum sounds made by drum blocks.


[size=4][b]Flooring[/b][/size]

To add flooring, create a tile layer called [b]Flooring [/b]and add tiles using a tilesheet with the [b]flooring.png[/b] file as its source.

There are 17 different types of flooring.


[size=4][b]Train Tracks[/b][/size]

To add train tracks, create a tile layer called [b]TrainTracks [/b]and add tiles using a tilesheet with the [b]traintracks.png[/b] file as its source.

To trigger a speed change on a specific tile, create an object layer called [b]TrainTracks[/b] and add an object called [b]TileData[/b] with a custom property called [b]Speed[/b], and set the value of the property to a positive integer.

To trigger automatic turns on forked tiles, use the [b]TrainTracks[/b] object layer as above and add an object called [b]TileData[/b] with a custom property called [b]Switches[/b].

The value for the Switches property should be a comma-separated list of [b]<FacingDirection>:<TurnDirectionList>[/b].

[b]<FacingDirection>[/b]  should be a number 0 - 3 (0 = up, 1 = right, etc.).
[b]
<TurnDirectionList>[/b] should be a list of numbers 0 - 3 as above separated by spaces.

E.g.:[b] 0:1 3,2:1 3[/b] means if the train enters the tile facing up (0) or down (2), the first time it should turn to the right of the screen (1) and the second time it should turn to the left of the screen (3).

You must have the [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/10927]Train Tracks[/url] mod installed to add train tracks.


[size=5][b]Technical[/b][/size]

Requires [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/2400/]SMAPI[/url], uses Harmony.

Compatible with [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/6338]Mod Updater[/url]﻿ for automatic updates.
